clauses.text: The Tenant shall pay a monthly rent of Rs. 18,000 on or before the 5th of every month by bank transfer.
clauses.explanation: Standard clause; no risk indicators found.

clauses.text: The security deposit of Rs. 1,08,000 shall be refunded after the Tenant vacates, less any deductions the Owner deems necessary.

findings.title: No deadline for returning the deposit
findings.explanation: The clause says the deposit will be returned but gives no deadline, so the landlord can delay it indefinitely.
findings.ask: Add a fixed timeline, e.g. 'refunded within 15 days of handing over possession'.

findings.title: Deposit is about 6.0× the monthly rent
findings.explanation: The security deposit equals roughly 6.0 months of rent. That is a lot of your money held by the landlord, and it is harder to recover in a dispute. For reference, India's Model Tenancy Act, 2021 suggests a cap of two months' rent for residential premises (it applies only in states that have adopted it).
findings.ask: Negotiate the deposit down to 2-3 months' rent, or ask for interest on the excess.

clauses.text: The Owner may terminate this agreement by giving the Tenant ten days' notice.

findings.title: Very short notice to vacate
findings.explanation: The landlord can end the tenancy with under a month's notice, which is very little time to find a new home.
findings.ask: Ask for at least one month's written notice.

clauses.text: This agreement shall stand automatically renewed for eleven months unless the Tenant gives notice sixty days before expiry.

findings.title: Automatic renewal
findings.explanation: The agreement renews by itself unless someone gives notice in time. Miss the window and you can be bound for another term, often at a higher rent.
findings.ask: Put the notice deadline in your calendar, or ask for renewal only by mutual written agreement.

clauses.text: On renewal the rent shall be increased by 12% of the last rent paid.

findings.title: Steep rent increase
findings.explanation: The rent rises by 10% or more, which is above typical annual increases (often around 5-10%).
findings.ask: Negotiate a lower cap (e.g. 5%) or a fixed rent for the first renewal.
